This combination — particularly *painless gross hematuria + sterile pyuria* — is highly associated with **urothelial malignancy**, especially in the renal pelvis or ureter, where tumor-induced mucosal irritation can cause bleeding and inflammatory cell influx without bacterial infection.  

Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) also commonly presents with painless hematuria and flank discomfort, but RCC typically does *not* cause significant pyuria — sterile pyuria is far more characteristic of urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) due to direct tumor-associated mucosal inflammation and sloughing.
